words.enDefinition: organized sports in which teams within the same university or institution play each other

examples.en: I signed up for intramural sports because I wanted to play without travelling every weekend.
examples.zh: 我想参加比赛又不想每周末外出，就报名参加了「校内体育比赛」。

examples.en: The university listed intramural sports beside club teams in its recreation guide.
examples.zh: 大学的文体活动指南并列介绍了「校内体育比赛」和社团运动队。

words.enDefinition: the rules that determine how contestants progress and how a winner is chosen

examples.en: The organizers changed the competition format so each team would play at least twice.
examples.zh: 主办方调整了「赛制」，让每支队伍至少打两场。

examples.en: The competition format was posted beside the registration desk before the teams arrived.
examples.zh: 各队到场前，「赛制」就张贴在了登记处旁边。

words.enDefinition: a sports league primarily organized for enjoyment and regular participation

examples.en: We chose the recreational league because we wanted a relaxed game after classes.
examples.zh: 我们选了「休闲体育联赛」，想课后轻松打一场。

examples.en: The recreational league offered weekend matches at a sports centre near our flat.
examples.zh: 「休闲体育联赛」在公寓附近的一家体育中心安排周末比赛。

words.enDefinition: a contest between teams or athletes from different colleges or universities

examples.en: Our rowing team entered an intercollegiate competition hosted by a university across town.
examples.zh: 我们的赛艇队参加了城另一头一所大学主办的「校际比赛」。

examples.en: The coach picked two first-year players for the intercollegiate competition this spring.
examples.zh: 教练选了两名一年级选手参加今年春季的「校际比赛」。

words.enDefinition: an informal game formed on the spot without a fixed roster

examples.en: We joined a pick-up game after seeing that the outdoor basketball court was free.
examples.zh: 发现户外篮球场空着后，我们参加了一场「现场临时组队的比赛」。

examples.en: I met two classmates during a pick-up game near the library last summer.
examples.zh: 去年夏天，我在图书馆附近的一场「现场临时组队的比赛」中认识了两名同学。

words.enDefinition: a list through which people without a team can find a place in a league

examples.en: I put my name on the free agent list before the volleyball registration deadline.
examples.zh: 排球报名截止前，我把名字加进了「无队伍球员名单」。

examples.en: Our captain found an extra player through the free agent list that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我们队长通过「无队伍球员名单」找了一位额外的球员。

collocations: sign up on the free agent list

words.zhGloss: 入队时未获体育奖学金的选手
words.enDefinition: in US college sports, an athlete who joins a team without an athletic scholarship
acceptedZhAnswers: 入队时未获体育奖学金的选手

examples.en: One of our starting players joined as a walk-on during her first year.
examples.zh: 我们一名首发球员在大一入队时是「未获体育奖学金的选手」。

examples.en: He earned a place as a walk-on after attending the team's open trial.
examples.zh: 参加球队的公开试训后，他以「入队时未获体育奖学金的选手」身份获得了一个名额。

words.enDefinition: the official or recorded list of people who are members of a team

examples.en: I checked the team roster before submitting our entries for the campus tournament.
examples.zh: 提交校园比赛报名之前，我核对了「球队名单」。

examples.en: The captain added my roommate to the team roster before the first match.
examples.zh: 第一场比赛前，队长把我室友加进了「球队名单」。

collocations: add a player to the team roster

words.enDefinition: the process of signing up an entire team for an event or league

examples.en: We completed team registration when the last player sent their student identification details.
examples.zh: 最后一名队员发来学生证信息后，我们完成了「团队报名」。

examples.en: The website displayed a separate deadline for team registration and individual signups that term.
examples.zh: 那学期，网站分别显示了「团队报名」和个人报名的截止日期。

words.enDefinition: the role or area of play that a player would most like to take

examples.en: The form asked for my preferred position before I joined the practice squad.
examples.zh: 我加入训练队以前，表格问我的「首选上场位置」。

examples.en: My teammate's preferred position changed after she played both roles during the weekend.
examples.zh: 我队友周末两个位置都打过之后，「首选上场位置」变了。

words.enDefinition: the players selected to begin a match

examples.en: The coach announced the starting lineup before our classmates arrived to watch the match.
examples.zh: 同学来观赛前，教练宣布了「首发阵容」。

examples.en: I was surprised to see our newest player in the starting lineup that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我没想到在「首发阵容」里看到了新队员。

words.enDefinition: the five basketball players selected to begin a game for one team

examples.en: Our starting five stood near the centre circle while waiting for the game to begin.
examples.zh: 我们的「篮球首发五人」在中圈附近等比赛开始。

examples.en: The coach changed the starting five after our usual point guard missed the bus.
examples.zh: 平时打控卫的队员没赶上公交，教练调整了「篮球首发五人」。

words.enDefinition: a secondary team within a sports club, often featuring developing or backup players

examples.en: She played for the reserve team during her first year at the university.
examples.zh: 她大学第一年在「预备队」效力。

examples.en: The reserve team had an early fixture before the main squad arrived that afternoon.
examples.zh: 首队当天下午来到之前，「预备队」有场更早的比赛。

words.enDefinition: to spend part or all of a game waiting without taking part

examples.en: I expected to sit on the bench until the start of the second half.
examples.zh: 我以为要一直「坐在替补席上」等到下半场开始。

examples.en: She preferred to play briefly rather than sit on the bench for the entire match.
examples.zh: 她宁可短暂上场，也不想整场都「坐在替补席上」。

collocations: have to sit on the bench
sit on the bench for a game
wait to play while you sit on the bench

words.enDefinition: to go onto the playing field to begin or resume play

examples.en: We watched both teams take the field just as our friends reached the stands.
examples.zh: 朋友们刚到看台，我们就看到两队「进入运动场比赛」。

examples.en: The referee waited for the visiting team to take the field after the break.
examples.zh: 休息结束后，裁判等客队「进入运动场比赛」。

words.enDefinition: a match played outside a formal league or competition for practice or enjoyment

examples.en: Our club arranged a friendly match with another college after the main season ended.
examples.zh: 正式赛季结束后，我们社团和另一所学院安排了一场「友谊赛」。

examples.en: I played my first friendly match before we chose the squad for the tournament.
examples.zh: 我们选出锦标赛阵容之前，我打了第一场「友谊赛」。

words.enDefinition: a schedule of matches planned for a team or competition

examples.en: I checked the fixture list to see which weekends would be free for travel.
examples.zh: 我看了「比赛日程表」，想知道哪几个周末能出去玩。

examples.en: The club updated its fixture list after two games had to be moved.
examples.zh: 两场比赛得改期后，俱乐部更新了「比赛日程表」。

words.enDefinition: a match between teams that counts toward their position in a league

examples.en: I missed my first league match because my seminar ran late that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午研讨课拖堂，我错过了自己的第一场「联赛比赛」。

examples.en: Our next league match was against a team made up of engineering students.
examples.zh: 下一场「联赛比赛」的对手是一支由工科学生组成的队伍。

words.enDefinition: the part of a tournament when teams first play in separate groups

examples.en: We watched two matches in the group stage before returning to campus for dinner.
examples.zh: 回学校吃晚饭前，我们看了两场「小组赛阶段」的比赛。

examples.en: The group stage ended on Friday, and the top teams played again the following week.
examples.zh: 「小组赛阶段」在周五结束，成绩靠前的球队下一周继续比赛。

words.enDefinition: the part of a tournament when a loss can end a team's participation

examples.en: We reached the knockout stage after a close match against the team from residence.
examples.zh: 和宿舍队打了一场比分很接近的比赛后，我们进入了「淘汰赛阶段」。

examples.en: The club moved its knockout stage games to the main sports hall for spectators.
examples.zh: 俱乐部把「淘汰赛阶段」的比赛移到主体育馆，方便观众观看。

words.enDefinition: a competition format in which every participant or team plays every other in a group

examples.en: The club used a round robin so everyone could play more than one match.
examples.zh: 俱乐部采用「循环赛」，这样每个人都能打不止一场。

examples.en: We consulted the round robin schedule before booking the courts for Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 订周六上午的球场之前，我们看了「循环赛」的赛程。

words.enDefinition: a diagram showing matchups and progression through the rounds of a tournament

examples.en: I found my team on the tournament bracket next to the gym entrance.
examples.zh: 我在体育馆入口旁的「淘汰赛对阵表」上找到了自己的队伍。

examples.en: The tournament bracket showed that the winners would meet again on Sunday afternoon.
examples.zh: 「淘汰赛对阵表」显示，获胜者周日下午会接着比赛。

words.enDefinition: a team given a tournament position based on its ranking or previous results

examples.en: Our group was drawn against a seeded team in the first match on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我们组周六的第一场比赛抽到了一支「种子队」。

examples.en: The seeded team had finished near the top of the league the previous year.
examples.zh: 那支「种子队」前一年在联赛里名列前茅。

words.enDefinition: a match or round that produces participants for the semifinals

examples.en: Our student team reached the quarter-final after winning its group on Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 学生队周六上午拿下小组第一后，进入了「四分之一决赛」。

examples.en: The quarter-final ended just in time for us to catch the last bus.
examples.zh: 「四分之一决赛」刚好结束，我们还赶得上末班车。

words.enDefinition: a contest that determines which participant or team goes through to the final

examples.en: We watched the semifinal from the side of the court after our game finished.
examples.zh: 自己的比赛打完后，我们在场边看了「半决赛」。

examples.en: My roommate had a class at the same time as the semifinal that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我室友上课正好和「半决赛」撞时间。

words.enDefinition: a table showing teams ranked by their results in a league

examples.en: The league table changed after our division played its postponed matches on Friday.
examples.zh: 我们组周五补打改期的比赛后，「联赛排名表」变了。

examples.en: I checked the league table before asking who our next opponents would be.
examples.zh: 问下一个对手是谁之前，我查了「联赛排名表」。

words.enDefinition: the status earned by winning a division within a sports league

examples.en: Our team secured the division title with a win in the last regular season game.
examples.zh: 我们队在常规赛最后一场获胜，拿到了「分区冠军头衔」。

examples.en: Several teams were still in contention for the division title when term ended.
examples.zh: 学期结束时，还有几支队伍在争夺「分区冠军头衔」。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled match that a team plays at the opponent's venue

examples.en: We travelled together for the away fixture at the college across the river.
examples.zh: 我们一起去河对岸的学院参加「客场比赛」。

examples.en: The team checked bus times before its away fixture on the last Saturday of term.
examples.zh: 学期最后一个周六有「客场比赛」，球队事先查了公交时刻。

words.enDefinition: two games scheduled for the same day, typically involving the same teams

examples.en: The field was reserved all afternoon for a doubleheader between two student softball teams.
examples.zh: 两支学生垒球队要打「同日连赛两场」的比赛，场地整个下午都预留了。

examples.en: I stayed for the second game of the doubleheader after my friend went home.
examples.zh: 朋友回家后，我留下看完了「同日连赛两场」的后一场。

words.enDefinition: to lose a game by failing to appear, refusing to continue, or breaking a rule

examples.en: Our team had to forfeit because too few players arrived by the deadline.
examples.zh: 截止时间前到场的人太少，我们队不得不「弃权认负」。

examples.en: The captain asked whether we would forfeit if the replacement bus arrived after kickoff.
examples.zh: 队长问，如果换乘的大巴在开赛后才到，我们是否会「弃权认负」。

words.enDefinition: a status showing a scheduled game will be played later

examples.en: The notice read game postponed after heavy rain left water on the outdoor court.
examples.zh: 大雨使室外球场积水后，通知显示「比赛已延期」。

examples.en: Our team chat showed game postponed before the college announced a new date.
examples.zh: 学院还没公布新日期，我们队的群聊已经显示「比赛已延期」。

words.enDefinition: a status showing play was stopped and the match did not finish

examples.en: The board displayed match abandoned after the floodlights went out during the second half.
examples.zh: 下半场泛光灯熄灭后，显示屏上出现了「比赛中途终止」。

examples.en: The website posted match abandoned without yet saying whether the score would count.
examples.zh: 网站发布了「比赛中途终止」，还没说原比分算不算。

words.enDefinition: a win awarded when the scheduled opponent cannot or does not compete

examples.en: We got a walkover when the opposing team couldn't field enough players on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五对方队员人数不够，我们「不战而胜」。

examples.en: The bracket marked our quarter-final as a walkover after the other pair withdrew.
examples.zh: 对方两人退赛后，对阵表将我们的四分之一决赛标为「不战而胜」。

words.enDefinition: a format in which the winner is determined by winning two of three games

examples.en: The table tennis club played best of three so everyone could finish before closing.
examples.zh: 乒乓球社采用「三局两胜」，这样关门前大家都能打完。

examples.en: We agreed to play best of three because we only had the court until six.
examples.zh: 球场只能用到六点，所以我们同意打「三局两胜」。

words.enDefinition: a series of wins in a row

examples.en: Our winning streak ended when we played the team from the other campus.
examples.zh: 我们跟另一校区的队交手时，「连胜纪录」结束了。

examples.en: The club's winning streak stretched through the first six matches of the season.
examples.zh: 俱乐部的「连胜纪录」持续了赛季开始的六场比赛。

words.enDefinition: points awarded for results that count toward a team's position in a league

examples.en: The draw earned enough league points to keep our team above the bottom spot.
examples.zh: 这场平局拿到的「联赛积分」够我们球队摆脱垫底。

examples.en: I checked the league points after both campus divisions played that weekend.
examples.zh: 两个校区组别那个周末都比完后，我查了「联赛积分」。

words.enDefinition: the number of goals scored minus the number conceded by a team

examples.en: Our team went ahead on goal difference even though both clubs had equal points.
examples.zh: 虽然两队积分一样，我们凭「净胜球数」排名领先。

examples.en: I worked out the goal difference using both scores from the previous round.
examples.zh: 我用上一轮的进球数和失球数算出了「净胜球数」。

words.enDefinition: a rule or extra contest used to decide between otherwise equal results

examples.en: The league used head-to-head results as a tie-breaker after the regular season ended.
examples.zh: 常规赛结束后，联赛用直接交手结果作为「平手判定办法」。

examples.en: I checked which tie-breaker applied before working out our team's position in the group.
examples.zh: 计算我们队的小组名次前，我查了适用的「平手判定办法」。

words.enDefinition: to score so that both sides have the same number of points or goals

examples.en: We had a chance to level the score before the last minute of play.
examples.zh: 比赛还剩最后一分钟前，我们有机会「扳平比分」。

examples.en: The other team managed to level the score soon after the break that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午休息过后不久，对方成功「扳平比分」。

words.enDefinition: a result in which neither side wins because their scores are equal

examples.en: The game ended in a draw after both teams missed chances near the end.
examples.zh: 两队快结束时都错过了机会，比赛以「平局」收场。

examples.en: We only needed a draw to qualify for the next round of the league.
examples.zh: 我们只要打成「平局」，就能进入联赛的下一轮。

words.enDefinition: a goal that makes the scores of two teams equal

examples.en: Our equaliser came just before the referee ended the first half of the match.
examples.zh: 上半场结束前，我们打进了「扳平比分的进球」。

examples.en: I nearly missed the equaliser because I was putting my coat back on.
examples.zh: 我当时正穿外套，差点错过「扳平比分的进球」。

words.enDefinition: the goal that gives a team the decisive lead in a match it wins

examples.en: My roommate scored the winning goal in the final match of the campus league.
examples.zh: 校园联赛最后一场，我室友打进了「制胜进球」。

examples.en: The supporters cheered for a long time after the winning goal that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚「制胜进球」打进后，球迷欢呼了很久。

words.enDefinition: the recorded result in points or goals at the end of a game

examples.en: I sent the final score to the friends who couldn't make the match.
examples.zh: 我把「终场比分」发给了没来观赛的朋友。

examples.en: The referee checked the final score against the score sheet on the table.
examples.zh: 裁判把「终场比分」和桌上的计分表作了核对。

words.enDefinition: to continue a game beyond regular playing time, typically because the score is tied

examples.en: We thought the basketball game might go into overtime with thirty seconds remaining.
examples.zh: 还剩三十秒时，我们觉得篮球赛可能会「进入加时赛」。

examples.en: I checked the bus schedule in case our final had to go into overtime.
examples.zh: 我查了公交时刻表，以防决赛得「进入加时赛」。

collocations: be likely to go into overtime

words.enDefinition: additional periods played after regular time to settle some tied football matches

examples.en: The final was still tied when regular play ended, so the teams played extra time.
examples.zh: 决赛常规时间结束时两队仍打平，于是踢了「足球加时赛」。

examples.en: Our captain scored during extra time, and we held the lead until the end.
examples.zh: 队长在「足球加时赛」时破门，我们把领先保持到了最后。

words.enDefinition: time added at the end of a half to allow for time lost during play

examples.en: The referee indicated stoppage time just as many of the students began to leave.
examples.zh: 不少学生刚开始离开，裁判就示意进入「伤停补时」。

examples.en: The winning goal came during stoppage time after neither team had scored for an hour.
examples.zh: 两队有一小时没进球，「伤停补时」阶段才出现制胜进球。

words.enDefinition: fair and respectful conduct toward other players and officials in sport

examples.en: The referee praised the sportsmanship both teams showed at the end of the match.
examples.zh: 裁判表扬了两队赛后都体现出的「体育精神」。

examples.en: Our club gives a prize for sportsmanship at the end of each campus tournament.
examples.zh: 我们社团每次校园锦标赛结束时都会颁发「体育精神」奖。

words.enDefinition: a line of opposing players greeting each other with handshakes after a game

examples.en: Both teams joined the handshake line after the last point of the final.
examples.zh: 决赛最后一分打完后，两队开始「赛后列队握手」。

examples.en: Our coach waited for the handshake line to end before speaking to the team.
examples.zh: 教练等「赛后列队握手」结束后才跟大家讲话。

words.enDefinition: one of the two long boundary lines on a football pitch

examples.en: My friend stood near the touchline to watch the last part of the match.
examples.zh: 比赛最后一段，朋友站在「足球场边线」附近看。

examples.en: The ball crossed the touchline just before the winger reached it that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午边锋就快追到球时，球越过了「足球场边线」。

words.enDefinition: the circle drawn at the midpoint of a sports playing area

examples.en: The players gathered inside the centre circle before the first kick of the game.
examples.zh: 比赛第一脚球开出前，队员们聚在「球场中圈」里。

examples.en: We could see the centre circle from our place halfway up the stands.
examples.zh: 我们坐在看台中段的位置，能看到「球场中圈」。

words.enDefinition: the rectangular area in front of a football goal where certain rules apply

examples.en: The player waited outside the penalty area while the goalkeeper collected the ball.
examples.zh: 守门员拿球时，那名队员在「足球禁区」外等着。

examples.en: I watched the ball roll slowly across the penalty area without anyone touching it.
examples.zh: 我看见球慢慢滚过「足球禁区」，没有人碰到。

words.enDefinition: the line along the entire end of a football pitch, on which the goal is placed

examples.en: The officials checked whether the entire ball had crossed the goal line before stopping play.
examples.zh: 叫停比赛前，裁判组确认整个球是否越过了「球门线」。

examples.en: The student keeper stood on the goal line as the other players got ready.
examples.zh: 其他队员准备时，那名学生守门员站在「球门线」上。

words.enDefinition: the mark on a football pitch from which a penalty kick is taken

examples.en: The referee pointed to the penalty spot and the crowd around us grew louder.
examples.zh: 裁判指向「点球点」，我们周围的观众声更大了。

examples.en: The player placed the ball on the penalty spot before waiting for the whistle.
examples.zh: 队员把球放在「点球点」上，然后等待哨响。

words.enDefinition: the kick that starts a period of play or restarts play after a goal

examples.en: We reached the field a few minutes before kick-off in the first campus final.
examples.zh: 第一场校园决赛「足球开球」前几分钟，我们到了球场。

examples.en: The team met beside the bench just before kick-off to hear the coach's reminder.
examples.zh: 「开球」前，队员们在替补席旁集合，听教练提醒了几句。

words.enDefinition: a football restart taken by throwing the ball from the touchline after the whole ball crosses it

examples.en: The referee awarded a throw-in after the ball went past the line beside us.
examples.zh: 球出了我们旁边的边线后，裁判判了「掷界外球」。

examples.en: Our team took a quick throw-in while the others were moving down the pitch.
examples.zh: 其他队员正沿球场向前移动，我们队快速「掷出界外球」。

words.enDefinition: a restart usually taken from a corner after the whole ball crosses the goal line without a goal, having last touched a defender

examples.en: The crowd got louder when our team won a corner kick near the end.
examples.zh: 比赛快结束时，我们队获得「角球」，观众声更大了。

examples.en: My roommate took the corner kick that led to the only goal of the match.
examples.zh: 正是室友发的「角球」，带来了整场唯一的进球。

words.enDefinition: a restart for the defending team usually given when the whole ball crosses the goal line without a goal, having last touched an attacker

examples.en: The goalkeeper took a goal kick after the shot went wide of the post.
examples.zh: 射门偏出门柱后，守门员开出「球门球」。

examples.en: We moved farther up the field while the other team prepared for a goal kick.
examples.zh: 对方准备开「球门球」时，我们往球场前方移动。

words.enDefinition: the player assigned to protect the goal and stop the other team from scoring

examples.en: Our goalkeeper spoke to each new player before the first match of the term.
examples.zh: 本学期第一场比赛前，我们的「守门员」和每个新队员都聊了几句。

examples.en: The goalkeeper caught the loose ball and waited for the players to move farther away.
examples.zh: 「守门员」接住了没人控制的球，等其他队员离开一些。

words.enDefinition: the horizontal bar connecting the top of the two goalposts

examples.en: The ball struck the crossbar and dropped just in front of the goal line.
examples.zh: 球打到「球门横梁」后，落在球门线正前方。

examples.en: A volunteer checked the crossbar while the teams warmed up on the other side.
examples.zh: 两队在另一侧热身时，一名志愿者检查了「球门横梁」。

words.enDefinition: a football offence committed when a player is in an offside position as a teammate plays or touches the ball and then becomes involved in active play

examples.en: We cheered too early because the referee called offside before the ball went in.
examples.zh: 我们欢呼太早了，因为球进门前裁判就吹了「越位」。

examples.en: The assistant referee raised a flag for offside while everyone waited near the touchline.
examples.zh: 大家在边线附近等着时，助理裁判举旗示意「越位」。

words.enDefinition: a kick awarded to a football team to restart play after an offence

examples.en: We could see the players get ready for the free kick just outside the area.
examples.zh: 我们能看见队员们准备踢禁区外的「任意球」。

examples.en: The referee awarded a free kick after stopping the match near the halfway line.
examples.zh: 裁判在中线附近叫停比赛后，判了一个「任意球」。

words.enDefinition: a free kick that cannot score directly unless another player touches the ball

examples.en: The referee signalled an indirect free kick after talking to the assistant near us.
examples.zh: 裁判和我们附近的助理裁判交谈后，示意判「间接任意球」。

examples.en: Our coach explained why the goal did not count from the indirect free kick.
examples.zh: 教练解释了为什么那个「间接任意球」直接进门不算分。

words.enDefinition: a kick from the penalty mark awarded for certain football offences

examples.en: I watched the penalty kick from behind the bench at the other end.
examples.zh: 我在另一端的替补席后面看了那个「点球」。

examples.en: Our captain scored a penalty kick to put the team ahead before the break.
examples.zh: 中场前，队长罚进「点球」，让我们队取得领先。

words.enDefinition: a series of alternating penalty kicks used to decide a tied football match

examples.en: The final went to a penalty shoot-out after both teams had scored in extra time.
examples.zh: 加时赛两队都有进球，决赛进入了「点球大战」。

examples.en: I stayed for the penalty shoot-out even though the campus bus was almost due.
examples.zh: 虽然校园公交快到了，我还是留下看了「点球大战」。

words.enDefinition: a card shown by a referee to formally caution a player

examples.en: The referee showed a yellow card after speaking briefly to the two team captains.
examples.zh: 裁判跟两名队长简短交谈后，出示了「黄牌警告」。

examples.en: The student player received a yellow card during the first half of the game.
examples.zh: 那名学生球员在上半场吃到「黄牌警告」。

words.enDefinition: a card shown by a referee to send a player off

examples.en: The crowd went quiet when the referee held up a red card near the touchline.
examples.zh: 裁判在边线附近举起「红牌」时，观众安静了下来。

examples.en: The team finished with fewer players after one defender received a red card.
examples.zh: 一名后卫被「红牌罚下」后，球队以更少的人数打完比赛。

words.enDefinition: a goal scored when a player puts the ball into their own team's net

examples.en: The match changed after an own goal put the visiting team ahead just before halftime.
examples.zh: 中场前，一个「乌龙球」让客队领先，比赛局势随之改变。

examples.en: The commentator checked the replay before recording it as an own goal that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，解说员查看回放后，才把它记为「乌龙球」。

collocations: go ahead through an own goal

words.enDefinition: a result in which a team or goalkeeper completes a game without conceding a goal

examples.en: Our goalkeeper kept a clean sheet in her first game for the team.
examples.zh: 我们的守门员第一次为球队参赛就「一球未失」。

examples.en: The club's third clean sheet of the month came in a difficult away match.
examples.zh: 俱乐部当月第三次「一球未失」是在一场艰难的客场比赛中。

words.enDefinition: three goals or other notable successes achieved by one player in a game

examples.en: My roommate scored a hat trick in the last football match of the term.
examples.zh: 本学期最后一场足球赛，室友上演了「帽子戏法」。

examples.en: The crowd applauded after the third goal completed a hat trick for the forward.
examples.zh: 第三个进球让前锋完成了「帽子戏法」，观众随即鼓掌。

words.enDefinition: the referee's whistle signalling the end of a football match

examples.en: We waited for the full-time whistle before our teammates joined us near the stand.
examples.zh: 我们等到「终场哨」响，队友才来和我们在看台旁会合。

examples.en: The score remained level until the full-time whistle late on Saturday afternoon.
examples.zh: 周六傍晚，比分一直打平到「终场哨」响。

words.enDefinition: the replacement of one player with another during a game

examples.en: The coach made a substitution a few minutes after the second half started.
examples.zh: 下半场开始几分钟后，教练进行了「换人调整」。

examples.en: We waited for the substitution while the referee confirmed which player was leaving.
examples.zh: 裁判确认哪位队员离场时，我们等着「换人调整」。

words.enDefinition: sports shoes with studs or similar grips for use on a football pitch

examples.en: I left my football boots near the door so I wouldn't forget them before practice.
examples.zh: 我把「足球鞋」放在门边，免得训练前忘带。

examples.en: The shop sold different football boots for artificial turf and natural grass fields.
examples.zh: 商店出售分别适用人造草和天然草场的「足球鞋」。

words.enDefinition: protective pieces worn over the front of the lower legs in sports

examples.en: I packed my shin guards in the side pocket before leaving for the match.
examples.zh: 出发去比赛前，我把「护腿板」放进了侧袋。

examples.en: The captain brought spare shin guards for players who had forgotten their own.
examples.zh: 队长带了备用「护腿板」，给忘带自己护腿板的球员。

words.enDefinition: a light vest worn to identify which team a player is on during practice

examples.en: I picked up a blue practice bib before joining the group near the goal.
examples.zh: 加入球门旁的队伍前，我拿了件蓝色的「训练分组背心」。

examples.en: The coach asked us to hand back each practice bib after the session ended.
examples.zh: 训练结束后，教练请我们交回每一件「训练分组背心」。

words.enDefinition: a shot going toward the goal that would score if it were not stopped

examples.en: The goalkeeper saved our first shot on target just before the break.
examples.zh: 中场休息前，守门员扑出了我们第一脚「射正」的球。

examples.en: Our only shot on target came in the opening minutes of the second half.
examples.zh: 我们唯一一次「射正」发生在下半场开始后的几分钟。

words.enDefinition: to strike one of the vertical goalposts, said especially of a shot

examples.en: It looked like the shot would hit the post before rolling out of play.
examples.zh: 那脚射门看起来会「击中门柱」，然后滚出界。

examples.en: We saw the ball hit the post just as the goalkeeper stepped forward.
examples.zh: 守门员刚向前迈步，我们就看见球「击中门柱」。

collocations: see a shot hit the post

words.enDefinition: an unopposed basketball shot taken from a marked line after certain fouls or violations

examples.en: My flatmate scored the last free throw before the opposing team called a timeout.
examples.zh: 对方叫暂停前，室友投进了最后一个「篮球罚球」。

examples.en: The new player waited behind the line before taking her first free throw that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，新队员在标线后等着，准备第一次「篮球罚球」。

words.enDefinition: a basketball shot worth three points when successfully made from outside the three-point line

examples.en: A late three-pointer brought our team within one point just before the final buzzer.
examples.zh: 终场哨前，一个比赛末段的「三分球」把我们和对手的差距缩到一分。

examples.en: My roommate attempted a three-pointer after catching the pass near the side of the court.
examples.zh: 室友在球场一侧接到传球后，尝试投了一个「三分球」。

words.enDefinition: the marked line behind which a player stands to take a free throw

examples.en: I could see the shooter step behind the free throw line from our seats.
examples.zh: 从座位上，我能看到投手退到「篮球罚球线」后面。

examples.en: The referee pointed to the free throw line after checking with the score table.
examples.zh: 裁判和记录台确认后，指向了「篮球罚球线」。

collocations: stand behind the free throw line
go to the free throw line
step up to the free throw line

words.enDefinition: a basketball shot taken close to the basket, typically following a step or jump

examples.en: Our team took the lead after a layup by the newest player that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，最新加入的队员一个「上篮」帮助我们取得领先。

examples.en: The defender moved aside just before she went up for the layup near the basket.
examples.zh: 她在篮筐附近起跳「上篮」之前，防守球员刚好让开。

words.enDefinition: a shot in which the basketball player releases the ball while in the air

examples.en: The club replayed the jump shot at the end of its highlight video.
examples.zh: 俱乐部在集锦视频结尾回放了那个「跳投」。

examples.en: He made a jump shot from just inside the line during practice on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二练习时，他在线内不远处命中一次「跳投」。

words.enDefinition: the start of a basketball game, traditionally with a jump ball

examples.en: I got to the gym a few minutes before tip-off after my evening seminar.
examples.zh: 晚间研讨课后，我在「篮球赛开场」前几分钟到达体育馆。

examples.en: Both teams had finished warming up well before tip-off in the afternoon game.
examples.zh: 下午那场比赛「篮球赛开场」前，两队早早就热完了身。

words.enDefinition: a way of starting or resuming basketball play in which an official tosses the ball between opposing players

examples.en: The referee called for a jump ball while the two players waited near centre court.
examples.zh: 裁判示意「跳球争球」时，两名球员在球场中央附近等着。

examples.en: Our team gained possession after the jump ball at the start of the game.
examples.zh: 比赛开始「跳球争球」后，我们队拿到了球权。

collocations: take part in a jump ball

words.enDefinition: a timer showing the time a basketball team has left to attempt a legal shot

examples.en: The shot clock showed just two seconds when the pass reached the corner.
examples.zh: 传球到角落时，「进攻计时器」只剩两秒。

examples.en: We could see the shot clock clearly from the seats above the far basket.
examples.zh: 从另一端篮筐上方的座位，可以清楚看到「进攻计时器」。

words.enDefinition: a successful shot released just before the buzzer ends a period of play

examples.en: The buzzer beater tied the score just as our friends were about to leave.
examples.zh: 朋友们刚准备走，一个「压哨命中」把比分扳平了。

examples.en: The campus channel replayed the buzzer beater at the end of its evening highlights.
examples.zh: 校园频道在晚间集锦的结尾重放了那个「压哨命中」。

words.enDefinition: to request a temporary break during play under the rules of the game

examples.en: Our coach decided to call a timeout after the team lost its lead.
examples.zh: 球队失去领先后，教练决定「叫暂停」。

examples.en: The captain asked the coach to call a timeout late in the fourth quarter.
examples.zh: 第四节接近尾声时，队长请教练「叫暂停」。

words.enDefinition: a basketball rule violation involving illegal contact by a player

examples.en: The scoreboard showed a personal foul next to the defender's number soon after halftime.
examples.zh: 中场后不久，记分牌在那名防守队员号码旁显示一次「个人犯规」。

examples.en: The referee explained the personal foul briefly before the players returned to their positions.
examples.zh: 队员回各自位置前，裁判简短解释了那次「个人犯规」。

words.enDefinition: to lose the right to keep playing after reaching the allowed number of fouls

examples.en: Our captain was worried she might foul out before the end of the fourth quarter.
examples.zh: 队长担心自己第四节结束前会「犯规次数满而离场」。

examples.en: It was the first time I had seen a player foul out in our league.
examples.zh: 这是我第一次在我们的联赛里看到有球员「犯规次数满而离场」。

words.enDefinition: a ball recovered after a missed basketball shot

examples.en: I watched the centre jump for the rebound after the shot bounced off the rim.
examples.zh: 投篮弹框后，我看着中锋跳起来抢「篮板球」。

examples.en: The guard collected the last rebound and held the ball until the buzzer sounded.
examples.zh: 后卫拿到最后一个「篮板球」，一直控制球到终场哨响。

words.enDefinition: a quick basketball attack before the defenders are in position

examples.en: We scored on a fast break after stopping the other team's attack near the basket.
examples.zh: 我们在篮下阻止对方进攻后，打成了一次「篮球快攻」。

examples.en: The fast break brought everyone to their feet in the small campus gym.
examples.zh: 这次「篮球快攻」让小小的校园体育馆里人人都站了起来。

words.enDefinition: the basketball player who usually directs the offence and handles the ball

examples.en: Our point guard spoke to the coach before the rest of the team arrived.
examples.zh: 其他队员到之前，我们的「控球后卫」和教练谈了谈。

examples.en: The point guard dribbled slowly toward the middle as the final minute began.
examples.zh: 最后一分钟开始时，「控球后卫」慢慢向中间运球。

words.enDefinition: a defence in which basketball players cover assigned areas of the court

examples.en: The coach used zone defense after the other team kept scoring close to the basket.
examples.zh: 对方连续在篮下得分后，教练采用了「区域联防」。

examples.en: We watched the team switch to zone defense in the middle of the final quarter.
examples.zh: 最后一节打到一半，我们看到球队改用「区域联防」。

words.enDefinition: a point that can end the current set if the player or team ahead wins it

examples.en: Our pair saved a set point before winning the next two rallies in doubles.
examples.zh: 双打中，我们这对组合先挽救了一个「盘点」，随后赢了接下来的两个回合。

examples.en: The player took a breath before serving on set point in the first set.
examples.zh: 第一盘打到「盘点」时，球员发球前深吸了一口气。

words.enDefinition: a point on which the player or team ahead can win the whole match

examples.en: The scores were close until our team finally reached match point in the third set.
examples.zh: 比分一直很接近，直到我们队在第三盘拿到「赛点」。

examples.en: I missed the match point because a friend walked in front of my seat.
examples.zh: 朋友从我座位前经过，我错过了「赛点」。

words.enDefinition: a tennis point that gives the receiving player a chance to win the server's game

examples.en: Our teammate saved a break point before holding her serve in the opening set.
examples.zh: 队友首盘挽救了一个「破发点」，保住了自己的发球局。

examples.en: The return went long when he had break point late in the second set.
examples.zh: 第二盘后段他拿到「破发点」时，回球出了底线。

words.enDefinition: a special scoring game used to decide a tied set or, under some competition rules, a tied match in tennis

examples.en: We played a tiebreak after the teams reached six games each in the final set.
examples.zh: 决胜盘打成六比六后，我们打了「平分决胜局」。

examples.en: The final tiebreak took longer than I expected because the points were so close.
examples.zh: 最后的「平分决胜局」比分咬得很紧，比我预期的打得久。

words.enDefinition: a tennis score at which both sides have won at least three points and are level

examples.en: The umpire called deuce after the return landed just inside the line at the back.
examples.zh: 回球落在底线内一点，主裁报出「网球局内平分」。

examples.en: Our doubles game went back to deuce three times before either team won it.
examples.zh: 那局双打三次回到「网球局内平分」，才有一队拿下该局。

words.enDefinition: a way of winning a tennis match without losing a set

examples.en: My classmate won in straight sets even though the second set was very close.
examples.zh: 虽然第二盘打得很接近，同学还是「未失一盘」赢得比赛。

examples.en: The college pair lost in straight sets but saved several set points along the way.
examples.zh: 学院这对组合「一盘没赢」就输了，不过过程中挽救了几个盘点。

words.enDefinition: the final set played to determine the winner after earlier sets are tied

examples.en: We changed courts before beginning the deciding set on the sunny side of campus.
examples.zh: 在校园向阳的一侧开打「决胜盘」前，我们换了球场。

examples.en: The deciding set began later because both players took a short break first.
examples.zh: 两名球员先进行短暂休息，因此「决胜盘」晚些开始。

words.enDefinition: the boundary line at the back of a tennis court or similar playing area

examples.en: I watched the ball land close to the baseline in the late afternoon light.
examples.zh: 下午晚些时候的光线下，我看到球落在「球场底线」附近。

examples.en: The player waited just behind the baseline before returning the next serve that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，球员在「球场底线」后等着接下一个发球。

words.enDefinition: one of the marked areas into which a legal tennis serve must land

examples.en: His first serve landed in the service box close to the centre line.
examples.zh: 他的一发落在「发球区」内，靠近中线。

examples.en: I checked the lines of the service box before we began our practice match.
examples.zh: 练习赛开始前，我核对了「发球区」的界线。

words.enDefinition: the first of the two serving attempts normally allowed at a tennis point

examples.en: My first serve went into the net during the opening game on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二开场局中，我的「第一发球」下网了。

examples.en: She hit a strong first serve that the other player could barely reach.
examples.zh: 她的「第一发球」很有力，对方几乎够不到。

words.enDefinition: the additional serve permitted when the first one at a tennis point is a fault

examples.en: I watched the second serve land near the line after her first went long.
examples.zh: 她一发出界后，我看见「第二发球」落在界线附近。

examples.en: My doubles partner paused before her second serve while someone retrieved the first ball.
examples.zh: 有人去捡一发的球，我的双打搭档等了一下才发「第二发球」。

words.enDefinition: a volleyball serve that directly scores a point

examples.en: The team celebrated a service ace at the start of the volleyball set.
examples.zh: 排球这局刚开始，队员就为一次「发球直接得分」庆祝。

examples.en: Our player delivered a service ace after the returner moved farther to the left.
examples.zh: 接球人往左移动一些之后，我们的队员「发球直接得分」。

words.enDefinition: two unsuccessful serving attempts in a tennis point, which loses that point

examples.en: The double fault gave our opponents a point at the end of the game.
examples.zh: 局末的「双误」让对方得了一分。

examples.en: I took longer before my next serve because I had just made a double fault.
examples.zh: 我刚打了一个「双误」，下次发球前多等了一会儿。

collocations: lose a point on a double fault

words.enDefinition: a long sequence of hits between opposing players before the point ends

examples.en: The two pairs played a long rally before the ball finally went past the line.
examples.zh: 球终于出界前，两对选手打了一个「长回合对打」。

examples.en: I lost track of the score during a long rally in our afternoon game.
examples.zh: 下午那场比赛的一次「长回合对打」里，我忘了比分。

words.enDefinition: a shot played on the same side of the body as the racket hand

examples.en: Her forehand landed just inside the line during our last practice game that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午最后一场练习赛，她的「正手击球」落在线内一点。

examples.en: I changed direction with a forehand after my opponent moved closer to the net.
examples.zh: 对方靠近球网后，我用一次「正手击球」改变了球的方向。

words.enDefinition: a shot played on the opposite side of the body from the racket hand

examples.en: My backhand went long when the ball came across the court too quickly.
examples.zh: 球横过球场来得太快，我的「反手击球」飞出了底线。

examples.en: I saw the player use a backhand from near the far corner of the court.
examples.zh: 我看见那名球员在球场远端角落附近打出一记「反手击球」。

words.enDefinition: a soft shot that lands just beyond the net, away from an opponent

examples.en: She played a drop shot when her opponent was still near the baseline.
examples.zh: 对手还在底线附近时，她打了一个「放短球」。

examples.en: I reached the drop shot just as the ball was dropping toward the court.
examples.zh: 球快落地时，我刚好赶上了那个「放短球」。

words.enDefinition: the light object with a skirt of feathers or plastic hit in badminton

examples.en: We found a shuttlecock under the bench after our first badminton game that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午羽毛球第一场结束后，我们在长凳下找到一个「羽毛球」。

examples.en: My classmate picked up the shuttlecock and handed it back to the server.
examples.zh: 同学捡起「羽毛球」，交还给发球人。

words.enDefinition: the small flat implement a player uses to hit a table tennis ball

examples.en: The club lent me a table tennis bat for the lunch break tournament.
examples.zh: 社团借给我一把「乒乓球拍」，参加午休时的小比赛。

examples.en: I borrowed a table tennis bat after leaving mine in the campus locker.
examples.zh: 我把自己的拍子落在校园储物柜里了，就借了一把「乒乓球拍」。

collocations: rubber on a table tennis bat

words.enDefinition: a doubles event in which each pair typically consists of one woman and one man

examples.en: The club added a mixed doubles event to the weekend tennis schedule last month.
examples.zh: 上个月，社团在周末网球赛程里加了一项「混合双打」。

examples.en: I entered mixed doubles with a classmate who had never played in the tournament.
examples.zh: 我和一位没参加过该锦标赛的同学一起报名了「混合双打」。

words.enDefinition: the volleyball player who usually delivers the ball to a hitter

examples.en: Our setter moved closer to the net as the ball came across the court.
examples.zh: 球从场地另一侧过来时，我们的「排球二传手」移到更靠近球网的地方。

examples.en: The coach introduced the new setter before we started the afternoon practice.
examples.zh: 下午训练开始前，教练介绍了新来的「排球二传手」。

words.enDefinition: a defensive specialist who replaces back-row players in volleyball

examples.en: I recognised the libero by the different colour of her shirt during the game.
examples.zh: 比赛中，我凭她不同颜色的球衣认出了「排球自由人」。

examples.en: Our libero helped keep the rally going after the ball came over unexpectedly.
examples.zh: 球出乎意料地飞过来后，我们的「排球自由人」帮球队把回合继续了下去。

words.enDefinition: a volleyball attacker who usually hits from the left side of the front row

examples.en: The outside hitter scored the point that ended the longest rally of the set.
examples.zh: 「排球主攻手」拿下了一分，结束了该局最长的对打。

examples.en: A friend from my statistics class played outside hitter for the visiting college team.
examples.zh: 我统计课上的一个朋友担任来访学院队的「排球主攻手」。

words.enDefinition: a volleyball player whose front-row role includes blocking and attacking near the centre

examples.en: Our middle blocker waited near the centre of the net during the long rally.
examples.zh: 长回合对打时，我们的「排球副攻手」等在球网中央附近。

examples.en: The team introduced its youngest middle blocker before the first match that afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午首场比赛前，球队介绍了最年轻的「排球副攻手」。

words.enDefinition: a defensive contact that keeps an opponent's attack in play

examples.en: A difficult volleyball dig gave our team another chance in the final rally.
examples.zh: 艰难地完成一次「排球防守救球」后，我们队在最后一个回合又有了机会。

examples.en: The crowd clapped when the volleyball dig kept the ball in play that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，一次「排球防守救球」让比赛得以继续，观众鼓起掌来。

words.enDefinition: the order in which volleyball players change positions around the court

examples.en: The referee checked our rotation order before allowing the next serve to go ahead.
examples.zh: 裁判查了我们的「排球轮转顺序」，才允许下一球发出。

examples.en: Our coach explained the rotation order before everyone went back out on the court.
examples.zh: 所有人回到场上之前，教练解释了「排球轮转顺序」。

words.enDefinition: an official responsible for certain calls about lines on a sports court or field

examples.en: The line judge indicated that the serve had landed just outside the court.
examples.zh: 「司线员」示意发球落在场地边线外一点。

examples.en: Our club asked me to be a line judge for the first doubles match.
examples.zh: 我们社团请我担任第一场双打比赛的「司线员」。

words.enDefinition: the order in which members of a baseball or softball team come up to bat

examples.en: I checked the batting order before walking to the bench beside the field.
examples.zh: 走去场边的替补席前，我看了「击球棒次」。

examples.en: The student coach posted our batting order before the softball game started in the park.
examples.zh: 公园里的垒球赛开始前，学生教练张贴了我们的「击球棒次」。

words.enDefinition: a baseball hit that allows the batter to score by rounding all the bases

examples.en: The college team cheered when its newest player hit a home run on Saturday.
examples.zh: 周六，学院队最新加入的队员打出一个「本垒打」，全队欢呼起来。

examples.en: We missed the home run because we were still walking to the stands.
examples.zh: 我们还在走去看台的路上，错过了那个「本垒打」。

words.enDefinition: a baseball outcome when the batter receives a third strike

examples.en: The crowd applauded the pitcher after the strikeout on the last pitch of the inning.
examples.zh: 这一局最后一球造成「三振」后，观众为投手鼓掌。

examples.en: The score sheet recorded a strikeout beside the first batter's name that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，计分表在第一位击球手的名字旁记了一次「三振」。

words.enDefinition: additional innings played when a baseball or softball game is still tied

examples.en: The game went into extra innings while people were checking the last bus schedule.
examples.zh: 大家正查末班车时，比赛进入了「棒球延长局」。

examples.en: We stayed for extra innings because my friend was playing in the outfield.
examples.zh: 朋友在外野上场，我们留着看完了「棒球延长局」。

words.enDefinition: a shirt worn by members of a sports team when they play

examples.en: I wore my team jersey to class before the last match of the season.
examples.zh: 赛季最后一场比赛前，我穿着「球队球衣」去上课。

examples.en: The captain gave me a clean team jersey after I forgot to bring mine.
examples.zh: 我忘了带球衣，队长给了我一件干净的「球队球衣」。

words.enDefinition: a player who delivers the ball to the batter in cricket

examples.en: The bowler walked back to her mark while our team watched from the boundary.
examples.zh: 「板球投球手」走回她的起投点，我们队在边界旁看着。

examples.en: Our new bowler met the rest of the cricket team before the afternoon match.
examples.zh: 下午比赛前，我们新的「板球投球手」和板球队其他队员见了面。

words.enDefinition: the cricket fielder positioned behind the batter's wicket to receive balls

examples.en: I could see the wicketkeeper from the bench beside the student sports field.
examples.zh: 从学生运动场旁的长椅，我能看见「板球守门员」。

examples.en: The wicketkeeper picked up her gloves before heading onto the field that Saturday.
examples.zh: 那个周六，「板球守门员」拿上手套走进了球场。

words.enDefinition: the marked line in front of the wicket that helps define a batter's ground

examples.en: Our coach showed us the popping crease before the first cricket game of term.
examples.zh: 本学期第一场板球赛开始前，教练给我们指了「板球击球线」。

examples.en: I could see the white popping crease clearly from the shade by the pavilion.
examples.zh: 我坐在看台旁的阴凉处，能清楚看见白色的「板球击球线」。

words.enDefinition: the area beyond either goal line where a team can score a touchdown

examples.en: Our seats were behind the end zone opposite the main college entrance that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午，我们的座位在学院主入口对面的「美式橄榄球端区」后面。

examples.en: The crowd stood when the runner approached the end zone late in the game.
examples.zh: 比赛后段，持球跑的球员接近「美式橄榄球端区」时，观众站了起来。

collocations: catch the ball in the end zone

words.enDefinition: a score in American football made by legally carrying the ball across the opponents' goal line or gaining legal possession in their end zone

examples.en: The college crowd cheered when our team scored a touchdown before the break.
examples.zh: 我们队在中场前完成了「美式橄榄球达阵」，学院的观众欢呼起来。

examples.en: I nearly missed the touchdown because my classmates arrived just as the play began.
examples.zh: 这次进攻刚开始时同学才到，我差点错过「美式橄榄球达阵」。

words.enDefinition: a score in American football from kicking the ball over the crossbar between the uprights

examples.en: The team tried a field goal just before halftime, but the kick went wide.
examples.zh: 半场结束前，球队尝试「美式橄榄球射门得分」，但球踢偏了。

examples.en: The kicker's field goal cut the lead before both teams went in at halftime.
examples.zh: 两队中场休息前，踢球手的「美式橄榄球射门得分」缩小了分差。

words.enDefinition: the first play opportunity in a new series of downs in American football

examples.en: The crowd applauded when the college team earned a first down in the second quarter.
examples.zh: 第二节，学院球队拿到新的「美式橄榄球首档」，观众鼓掌了。

examples.en: I looked at the board after the announcer said we had a first down.
examples.zh: 播报员说我们拿到了「美式橄榄球首档」，我就看向记分牌。

words.enDefinition: the imaginary line through the ball's starting position before a play from scrimmage

examples.en: The players gathered near the line of scrimmage just before the next play began.
examples.zh: 下一档开始前，队员们在「美式橄榄球开球线」附近集合。

examples.en: I could see the line of scrimmage from my seat near the campus band's section.
examples.zh: 我坐在校园乐队分区旁，能看到「美式橄榄球开球线」。

collocations: line up at the line of scrimmage
